name: Vehicle mix and per-class parameters for Indian (Bengaluru) urban traffic
type: dataset / standard values (vehicle dimensions, kinematics, gaps and traffic composition)
maintainer: CSIR-CRRI (Indo-HCM 2017); Indian Roads Congress (IRC:106-1990 urban PCU); Chandra and Kumar (IIT Roorkee, J. Transp. Eng. 2003) dimension table reproduced in NPTEL; IIT Madras / TU Dresden (Kanagaraj, Treiber, Asaithambi, Agrawal) Chennai trajectory studies; DataCorp Traffic (Silk Board counts, reported by Traffic Infratech); WRI India (Bengaluru fleet share).
first_release: 1990 (IRC:106); 2003 (Chandra and Kumar dimension/PCU method); 2015 (Kanagaraj et al. Chennai trajectory data); 2017 (Indo-HCM); 2018 (Kanagaraj-Treiber calibrated per-class IDM); 2026 (Agrawal et al. Chennai UAV per-class statistics).
last_activity: arXiv 2608.00602 submitted 1 August 2026 (Chennai Saidapet UAV dataset recorded 26 June 2023).
licence: Indo-HCM and IRC codes: copyrighted publications (IRC codes sold by IRC; Indo-HCM distributed by CSIR-CRRI). Papers: publisher copyright; arXiv preprints non-exclusive distribution licence. Numbers themselves can be used as model parameters with citation.
code_availability: No code. Values are tabulated in papers and manuals (links). Indo-HCM 2017 full text is circulated as PDF (searchable copy on Scribd; official CSIR-CRRI distribution) - the dimension table (Section 1.3 'Vehicle Types and Their Dimensions') was not directly retrieved in this research.
maintenance_health: Indo-HCM 2017 is the latest edition; no update found. Research values are refreshed by the IIT Madras / TU Dresden group (2015, 2018, 2024, 2026). Bengaluru-specific classified counts are scarce in open literature; the best open evidence is a junction count at Silk Board (2019/2020) and city fleet shares.
mixed_traffic_support: Indian urban arterials carry two-wheelers (57-71% of vehicles), cars (20-27%), auto-rickshaws (5-12%), buses (2-4%) and small shares of LCV/HCV and bicycles on the same carriageway with largely ignored lane markings; the simulator must support at least 5 classes: two-wheeler, car, auto-rickshaw, bus/HCV, LCV (bicycle optional).
non_lane_behaviour: Observed on Chennai six-lane arterial: 'three nominal lanes, which are largely ignored' (Kulkarni et al.). Lateral speed in congestion: SD two-wheeler 0.25 m/s (P90 0.30 m/s, max 2.15 m/s), auto 0.15 m/s, car 0.09 m/s, LCV 0.12, HCV 0.10; lateral acceleration SD TW 0.18 m/s2, AR 0.11, car 0.08, HCV 0.10 m/s2 (Agrawal et al. 2026). At area density below ~0.05 veh/m2 lateral velocities span -0.3 to 0.6 m/s; above ~0.15 veh/m2 lateral motion is suppressed.
seepage_filtering_support: Smaller vehicles filter through queues; two-wheeler standstill gap median 0.55 m vs car 1.32 m, enabling tighter packing (Agrawal et al. 2026). Two-wheeler share in high-density states reached 73.2-82.7%.
per_class_parameters: DIMENSIONS (length x width, m). A) Chennai UAV 2023, measured, median (mean) [Agrawal et al. 2026, Table 3]: two-wheeler 2.01 x 0.73 (2.02 x 0.74); car 4.42 x 1.85 (4.46 x 1.85); auto-rickshaw 2.92 x 1.35 (2.92 x 1.35); LCV 5.66 x 2.23 (5.89 x 2.27); HCV incl. buses 11.97 x 2.92 (11.56 x 2.90). B) Chandra and Kumar 2003 PCU-method table (reproduced by NPTEL; widely reused and believed to match Indo-HCM/IRC practice [uncertain]): car/jeep/van 3.72 x 1.44 (area 5.39 m2); bus 10.10 x 2.43 (24.74); truck 7.50 x 2.35 (17.62); LCV/mini bus 6.10 x 2.10 (12.81); multi-axle truck 12.0 x 2.35 (28.60); scooter/motorbike 1.87 x 0.64 (1.20); pedal cycle 1.90 x 0.45 (0.85); auto/tempo 3.20 x 1.40 (4.48). C) Kanagaraj-Treiber 2018 calibrated model values: motorcycle 1.8 x 0.6; car 4.2 x 1.7; bus 10.3 x 2.1; auto-rickshaw 2.6 x 0.9 [uncertain]. DESIRED SPEED / FREE SPEED: Kanagaraj-Treiber IDM v0 ranges motorcycle 18-25 m/s (65-90 km/h), car 12-18 m/s (43-65 km/h), bus 10-14 m/s (36-50 km/h), auto-rickshaw printed '5-6 m/s' [uncertain]; max speeds observed in Chennai congestion: TW 14.84 m/s, car 14.81, AR 12.25, LCV 9.28, HCV 9.62 m/s. Space-mean speeds in the NPTEL worked example: car 8.34, 3-wheeler 8.52, 2-wheeler 7.70, LCV 6.83, HCV 6.05 m/s [uncertain units/context]. ACCELERATION / DECELERATION: Kanagaraj-Treiber IDM a = 2.0 m/s2 and b = 2.0 m/s2 for motorcycles, a = 1.0 and b = 1.0 m/s2 for car, bus and auto; bmax 9 m/s2. Observed longitudinal acceleration in congestion (Chennai 2023): SD TW 0.48, car 0.39, AR 0.40, LCV 0.38, HCV 0.37 m/s2; extremes about +/-3 m/s2 for all classes; P90 TW 0.57, car 0.46, AR 0.47 m/s2. SUMO generic defaults for reference (not Indian): motorcycle accel 6 / decel 10 m/s2, passenger 2.6 / 4.5, bus 1.2 / 4, truck 1.3 / 4, bicycle 1.2 / 3. TIME GAP AND STANDSTILL GAP (Chennai 2023 steady state, median / mean): TW 0.49 / 0.67 s and 0.55 / 0.73 m; car 1.21 / 1.34 s and 1.32 / 1.46 m; AR 0.81 / 0.92 s and 0.83 / 1.04 m; LCV 1.08 / 1.25 s and 0.99 / 1.20 m; HCV 1.57 / 1.86 s and 0.71 / 0.83 m (small samples for LCV/HCV). LATERAL CLEARANCE: Kanagaraj-Treiber lateral interaction scale 0.15 m (braking) and 0.30 m (steering), boundary 0.15-0.25 m; minimum lateral spacing distributions analysed by Agrawal et al. (values in figures, not tabulated in text) [uncertain]. PCU (static, urban): IRC:106-1990 values for two-wheeler 0.5/0.75, car 1.0, auto 1.2/2.0, LCV 1.4/2.0, bus/truck 2.2/3.7, cycle 0.4/0.5 at 5% / >=10% share [uncertain - recalled, not verified from primary text]; Indo-HCM 2017 uses dynamic PCU = (Vc/Vi)/(Ac/Ai) based on speed and projected area (Chandra method).
indian_calibration_evidence: Dimensions, gaps and kinematics measured on Chennai urban arterials with validated trajectory extraction (Saidapet UAV: detection precision 97%, recall 93%, MOTA 94%; mean absolute positional errors 0.04-0.07 m). Per-class IDM values calibrated by genetic algorithm and validated to within 20% on travel time and flows (Kanagaraj-Treiber 2018). Silk Board counts are raw counts, not used in any calibration.
calibration_dataset_used: Chennai Saidapet UAV dataset (26 June 2023, 09:30-10:30, 36 min, ~5,891 trajectories, 0.04 s); Chennai six-lane arterial video (Kanagaraj et al. 2015; 3016 vehicles in 30 min); Silk Board Junction, Bengaluru (DataCorp Traffic, March 2019 and 2020 working-day peak hour). Openness: Chennai datasets not confirmed open [uncertain]; Silk Board counts only published as a news article.
calibration_method: Trajectory-derived statistics with steady-state leader-follower filter (relative speed within deadband, |acc| < 0.2 m/s2, persistence) for time gaps; stopped state |v| <= 0.01 m/s for >= 3 s for standstill gaps; heading-corrected bounding boxes for dimensions. Genetic algorithm on macroscopic measures for IDM per class.
max_density_tested: Chennai 2023: area density up to ~0.33 veh/m2 (two-wheeler share 82.7%); congested Chennai MTM validation: 450 motorcycles/km + 225 cars/km + 35 buses/km + 80 autos/km.
validation_against_field_case: Bengaluru Silk Board Junction peak-hour classified counts (composition only). Per-class kinematics only from Chennai.
network_import: Not applicable to this item beyond composition: vehicle mix should be specified per entry link as class shares, since mixes differ by corridor (Silk Board 65% TW vs Chennai 57-71%).
demand_input_formats: Recommended: demand per origin link as total veh/h plus a class-share vector, e.g. Bengaluru default {two-wheeler 0.65, car 0.22, auto-rickshaw 0.055, bus 0.04, LCV/other 0.035} derived from Silk Board 2019 peak hour (15,507 veh: TW 10,113 = 65.2%, car 3,454 = 22.3%, auto 845 = 5.4%, bus 632 = 4.1%, other ~463 = 3.0%); 2020 count (20,074 veh): TW 67.1%, car 21.3%, auto 5.6%, bus 1.8%, other ~4.1%. Cars at Silk Board 2019 were 73% private / 27% taxi. Other Indian arterial mixes: Chennai six-lane arterial 2015: TW 57%, car 27%, three-wheeler 12%, bus 3%, light truck 1%, heavy truck 0.3%; Chennai Saidapet 2023: TW 70.84%, car 20.37%, auto 7.32%, LCV 0.54%, HCV 0.93%. Bengaluru registered fleet: two-wheelers ~69%, buses < 1% (WRI India) - fleet share, not road share.
data_access: Chennai 2023 values: arXiv 2608.00602 PDF (free). Kanagaraj-Treiber 2018: arXiv 1805.05076 (free). Chandra-Kumar dimension table: NPTEL course page (free); original ASCE paper paywalled. Indo-HCM 2017: CSIR-CRRI publication, unofficial searchable copy on Scribd; IRC:106-1990: purchase from IRC. Silk Board: Traffic Infratech article (free). Bengaluru CTTP (KUIDFC 2011) on data.opencity.in contains mid-block volume tables (Table 3.1) but could not be retrieved here [uncertain].
reuse_mode: Use as data: ship a default vehicle-class table (dimensions, IDM parameters, lateral clearance, colour) and a default Bengaluru class mix in the scenario schema, with source citations.
effort_within_72_hours: 1-2 hours to encode the table and default mix as JSON plus per-class sampling (draw length/width from normal distributions with the published mean/SD, e.g. TW length 2.02 +/- 0.11 m, car 4.46 +/- 0.42 m). Cut: per-corridor calibration, dynamic PCU computation (report PCU with fixed static factors instead), bicycles and cycle-rickshaws unless a scenario needs them.
licence_constraint: Numbers are facts and can be used with citation. Do not redistribute Indo-HCM or IRC PDF text or tables verbatim; arXiv preprints are non-exclusive licence (cite, do not republish).
known_limitations: No open Bengaluru per-class kinematic dataset was found; all trajectory-based kinematics come from Chennai mid-block sections, so intersection behaviour (start-up acceleration, discharge headways) is not covered. Chennai 2023 kinematics are from congested states (mean speeds 2-2.5 m/s), so they under-represent free-flow desired speeds and maximum accelerations. LCV/HCV samples are small (13-19 pairs). Silk Board figures are a single junction, single peak hour, from a commercial firm's internal study reported in trade media; class 'others' is unreported. Dimension sources disagree (car 3.72 x 1.44 m in the 2003 table vs 4.46 x 1.85 m measured in 2023), reflecting fleet growth toward SUVs - older tables understate car size. The Kanagaraj-Treiber auto-rickshaw width 0.9 m and v0 '5-6 m/s' look inconsistent with measured 1.35 m width and observed 12 m/s maxima. IRC/Indo-HCM primary tables were not directly accessed.
documented_failures: IHCM PCU values have been criticised as too optimistic and not reflecting actual service conditions (IAENG WCE 2017 paper). Using a single static PCU ignores that PCU depends on composition and speed (motivation for Chandra's dynamic PCU).
validation_approach: Field measurement: UAV trajectories with manual ground-truth validation of extraction accuracy; manual video classified counts; GA-calibrated simulation compared against observed travel times and flows.
takeaway_for_our_build: Define five default classes with these parameters (L x W m; IDM v0 km/h, T s, s0 m, a m/s2, b m/s2; min lateral clearance m): two-wheeler 2.0 x 0.75; 60; 0.5; 0.55; 2.0; 2.0; 0.2 | car 4.45 x 1.85; 50; 1.2; 1.3; 1.2; 1.5; 0.3 | auto-rickshaw 2.9 x 1.35; 40; 0.8; 0.8; 1.0; 1.5; 0.25 | bus 11.5 x 2.6; 40; 1.5; 1.5; 0.8; 1.2; 0.4 | LCV 5.9 x 2.25; 45; 1.2; 1.0; 1.0; 1.5; 0.3 (v0 and clearances are engineering choices interpolated from the cited ranges, not single published values). Default Bengaluru mix: TW 65%, car 22%, auto 6%, bus 4%, LCV 3% (Silk Board 2019). Make every value editable per scenario, sample dimensions from distributions rather than fixed means, display the source next to each default, and report outputs per class and in PCU using Chandra's area-speed method so users can compare to Indo-HCM practice.
